scope: Week 1 convergence draft: SARS primary trade and updated driver evidence accepted for reporting; provincial estimates separate; accounting, model calibration and Vopak capture remain open. Supplied master and slide order retained.

titles.2: Size the fuel market, reconcile supply, then test Vopak access
titles.3: Three provinces account for 69% of reported fuel sales; the top two contain Vopak’s storage facilities
titles.4: Reported fuel sales were broadly steady through 2022, despite the pandemic dip
titles.5: Diesel drives import volumes, while conflicting reports leave 2024 sales unresolved
titles.6: Provincial demand is known; its supply origin still needs evidence
titles.7: Activity trends show potential demand shifts; fuel used per unit of activity still needs validation
titles.8: Refinery capacity has fallen; redevelopment remains conditional
titles.9: Transport cost shapes the market Durban and Lesedi can reach
titles.10: Compare Durban, Matola and Walvis Bay for the same inland customer
titles.11: Separate market demand, accessible volume and unique Vopak deliveries
titles.12: Compare regional demand with Vopak’s published storage footprint
titles.13: The illustrative additional opportunity is 5.5 billion litres a year
titles.14: Durban leads the published storage subset
titles.15: Translate additional fuel flows into a preliminary inventory requirement

findings: Demand is concentrated
Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and Western Cape account for 68.6% of reported 2022 petrol/diesel sales.
Four reporting regions
Eastern coast: EC/KZN. Inland: GP/FS/LP/MP/NW. Western coast: WC. Other: NC. Boundaries are reporting groups.
Sales locate the historical market
Colours show provincial sales totals, not density or customer catchments. Only Durban and Lesedi are labelled; competitor detail is on pages 12 and 14.
3.action: Nigel: confirm customer markets for Durban and Lesedi. Manish: retain the observed 2022 map; present later estimates separately with national-source flags.

findings: Gauteng remains the largest market
The reported series places Gauteng above the other provinces throughout 2013–2022. Volumes differ across the smaller markets.
Later provinces are estimates
2024 petrol estimates: Gauteng 3.47, KZN 1.47, Western Cape 1.41 bn L. These hold 2022 shares; no later observed provincial sales were found.
Historical differences are traced
The analyst branch corrects the 2013 parser. Sources differ in 2014/2015; 2018 district coverage is incomplete. Retain these flags.
4.action: Manish: reconcile source selections and retain estimate labels. Nigel: decide whether estimated petrol volumes belong in the outlook; diesel booking shares are less stable.

findings: Customs supports the trade selection
SARS records diesel imports of 10.793 and exports of 0.796 bn litres in 2024. Net imports are 9.997; use customs as the primary trade source.
Reported sales remain a proxy
FIASA reports petrol/diesel sales of 20.763 bn litres for 2024. Editions differ; this demand proxy remains unverified and is not imports plus exports.
Production and stocks remain open
Production and stocks remain unresolved. The proposed 3-4 bn litre diesel gap is a hypothesis, not measured consumption.
5.action: Manish: rebuild the balance CSV from SARS; match product, year, actual output and stock changes. Nigel: agree the sales selection and obtain customer/port evidence.

findings: Darker means lower transport cost
Cells show example road cost from Durban or Lesedi. The rate is illustrative and excludes fuel price, storage and pipeline tariffs.
Grey means unassessed
Grey areas have no assessed road connection under this illustration. They are not confirmed to be inaccessible.
A cost surface is a first screen
Pipeline and rail lines are context. Route capacity, product compatibility and customer rights still determine serviceable demand.
9.action: Nigel: select the first customer destination and cost threshold. Manish: replace example rates with dated route costs and access evidence.

findings: Vopak has a South African footprint
Durban and Lesedi are highlighted against 2022 provincial sales. Colour shows sales totals; it does not establish Vopak market dominance.
Matola has published fuel storage
Galp/IPG GIMTL lists 60,000 m³ of petrol/diesel tanks, plus 6,000 m³ LPG excluded here. N4 is the eastern inland comparison route.
Walvis has storage and handling
NAMCOR NOSF lists 75,000 m³ in total, including 65,000 m³ petrol/diesel. Trans-Kalahari is the western inland comparator.
10.action: Manish: verify available tanks, customer access and full delivered costs. Source Namibia/Mozambique demand before extending the heatmap; grey means unassessed.

findings: Count customer demand once
Example receipts of 2.8 at Durban and 2.0 at Lesedi include a shared 1.8 transfer. Unique demand served is therefore 3.0 bn litres.
Accessibility precedes opportunity sizing
Example catchment demand 14.5 → physically feasible 12.0 → commercial envelope 8.5. Each screen requires evidence.
Examples are separate from sales
These market volumes illustrate the calculation. They are not the reported 2022 regional totals or actual Vopak deliveries.
11.action: Nigel: request customer deliveries, destinations and transfer records. Manish: calculate unique served demand before estimating additional access.

findings: Inventory days set working stock
At the illustrative 5.5 bn litres/year, 14 days needs about 211 thousand m³. More inventory days require more stock.
Existing tanks may cover part
Usable spare tanks may absorb this inventory. Published gross capacity does not establish spare petrol/diesel space.
Sizing needs an operating case
Test peak receipts, product segregation, tank heels and dispatch limits. This is a sensitivity, not an investment recommendation.
15.action: Nigel: confirm candidate flows and inventory policy. Manish and Henry: test usable spare tanks, peak flows and operating allowances before sizing new capacity.

findings: Capacity has fallen
Published capacity falls from 718 to 358 thousand bbl/day between 2020 and 2022. Redevelopment remains conditional.
Reported output is different
FY2024 Secunda output is 29.1 million barrels; Natref is 17.8 for Sasol’s share. Both cover all products and a year to June.
A product bridge is needed
Match product yields, calendar years and downtime before calculating import effects. Capacity does not measure actual output.
8.action: Manish: match operator output to product/year and document Natref ownership basis. Henry: review technical mechanisms. Nigel: agree refinery scenario timing.

overview_rows:
Demand baseline and regional market
2022 provinces are observed; 2023-2024 are estimated separately. Resolve source versions before forecasting.

Domestic supply and finished imports
SARS 2024 net diesel imports: 9.997 bn L. Match actual production, stocks and sales coverage; port allocation remains open.

Demand drivers
Monthly activity to Jul 2026; GDP Q2 2026; inland prices Oct 2026. Define activity-to-litres bridges before calibrating cases.

Refinery availability
Capacity history and reported operator output are distinct. Align fiscal/calendar years and product yields; redevelopment stays conditional.

Competing supply routes
Compare Durban, Matola and Walvis Bay for one customer. Test full route cost, capacity and customer access.

Vopak share and additional demand
Match unique deliveries to regional demand. Test additional volumes against physical and commercial access.

Storage and optional investment
Use published tanks as context. Assess additional services only after the incremental customer-flow case.
